title: When a Victorian pool barrier is needed and construction precautions
audience: Installers, builders' assistants and service workers on pool build sites in Victoria. The rules covered here are Victorian only.
learningOutcomes: State the barrier depth rule from the VBA consumer page, and check the construction requirements with the building surveyor.
Describe the site fencing and excavation precautions that the VBA Building Practice Note SP 01 sets out.
State the builder requirement and the 12-month and six-month time limits for pool and barrier building work.

instruction.heading: What the barrier must do
instruction.body: The Victorian Building Authority consumer page on pool safety barriers states that a barrier must be capable of containing water to a depth greater than 300 mm, and that a pool which cannot hold more than 300 mm of water is exempt. The same page says safety barriers must comply with AS1926.1-2012. Check the building requirements with the building surveyor before starting, and record the barrier position with the building surveyor.

instruction.heading: Site fencing and excavation guarding
instruction.body: The VBA Building Practice Note SP 01 says excavation of a pool shell can be a hazard. The site fencing considered under regulation 116 must include provisions to restrict access during excavation, during construction, and once the pool can contain water. Where the relevant building surveyor decides protection work is required, it must be provided before and during construction. Check the building requirements, including site fencing, with the building surveyor before starting, and record the check.

instruction.heading: Builder type and time limits
instruction.body: The VBA consumer page says pools, spas and safety barriers must be constructed by a registered builder, or by an owner-builder who has an owner-builder certificate of consent. The VBA Building Practice Note SP 01 says building work for a swimming pool and barrier must commence within 12 months of the building permit's issue date and be completed within six months of the work commencing, citing regulations 53 and 54. Note the permit's issue date and the planned start date against these limits.

procedure: Check the building permit covers the pool and barrier, and note its issue date and the planned start date.
Check the building requirements, including site fencing, with the building surveyor before starting, and record the check.
Track the water level in the excavation or shell against the 300 mm depth in the VBA barrier rule, and record the barrier position with the building surveyor.
Report any missing or shifted precaution to the builder and the building surveyor straight away.

workedExamples.situation: A fibreglass pool shell is set in a backyard and the crew starts filling it. The water is at 320 mm and no barrier has gone up around the pool zone yet.
workedExamples.reasoning: The water is at 320 mm, which is above the 300 mm depth in the VBA consumer page's barrier rule, so the barrier must be capable of containing that depth. Stop the filling, do not add more water, and report the barrier position to the builder and building surveyor before any further filling is considered.

equipmentAndPpe: Permit copy showing the barrier details
Water level marker for the shell or excavation
Site fence panels and fixings, as the permit specifies
Hard hat, safety boots and gloves for site work

commonErrors.error: Treating the 300 mm rule as the only building requirement for the barrier.
commonErrors.prevention: The VBA consumer page sets the 300 mm depth rule. Check the rest of the building requirements with the building surveyor and record the answer.

commonErrors.error: Starting excavation without checking the site fencing requirement.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the building requirements, including site fencing, with the building surveyor before starting.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The VBA Building Practice Note SP 01 says excavation of a pool shell can be a hazard, and that site fencing must restrict access during excavation, during construction, and once the pool can contain water. Keep the site fenced and check the access restriction with the building surveyor.

The VBA consumer page says pools, spas and safety barriers must be built by a registered builder, or by an owner-builder with an owner-builder certificate of consent. Registration is a licence-type requirement; this lesson does not grant it.

qualityStandard: The building requirements, including site fencing, are checked with the building surveyor before starting, and the check is recorded.
The water level is recorded against the 300 mm depth, and the barrier position is recorded and confirmed with the building surveyor.
documentationEvidence: Building requirements check record, with date and time, before starting
Water level and barrier check record
Building surveyor's written direction, where the permit or surveyor requires one
summary: According to the VBA consumer page, a pool barrier must be able to contain water deeper than 300 mm.
Check site fencing and excavation requirements with the building surveyor before starting.

Pools, spas and safety barriers must be built by a registered builder, or by an owner-builder with an owner-builder certificate of consent. Building work must commence within 12 months of the permit's issue date and be completed within six months of commencing.

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the VBA consumer page, what must a pool barrier be able to contain?
According to the VBA Building Practice Note SP 01, what must the site fencing considered under regulation 116 include?
options: Nothing, once the permit is issued and the builder may remove any fence and leave the site open
Provisions to restrict access during excavation, during construction and once the pool can contain water
A written agreement with the neighbours only and no change to the fencing at all on the site
A warning sign and a padlock on the gate of the whole site, the lot and the house today

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the VBA Building Practice Note SP 01, which time limit applies to building work on a pool and barrier?
options: Work may start up to 24 months after the building permit's issue date
Work must commence within 12 months of the building permit's issue date
Work may start at any stage, with no date tied to the permit
Work must be finished before the permit is issued

sourceReferences: Victorian Building Authority, Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Version 3, 26 September 2023), pool definition point only; rights: user-held; reworded (no copying). SP 02 does not cover barrier timing during construction, concrete pool filling, surveyor certificates, 14-day notices or time limits. The site-fencing and time-limit points come from Building Practice Note SP 01 (R4), and the 300 mm and builder points from the consumer page (R3).

Priority: the official VBA consumer page (R3) supports the 300 mm barrier depth, builder registration and AS1926.1-2012; SP 02 (R2) supports the pool definition of depth greater than 300 mm; Building Practice Note SP 01 (R4) supports the site fencing, Form 23 and time-limit points. UNCONFIRMED for other states and territories.

UNCONFIRMED: mandatory construction timing of the barrier, the exact date site fencing must be erected, the concrete pool filling certificate, the 14-day notice for a separate fencing contractor, the registration category or class for a given job; and registration and permit rules in other states.

officialReferences.title: Building practice notes: categories P to Z (Victorian Building Authority), swimming pool text
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary tool (WebFetch). The page does not contain Practice Note 05-2018 or its barrier, 300 mm, surveyor certificate or time-limit points. It says councils act as gatekeeper for compliance of safety barriers and that Part 9A of the Building Regulations 2018 consolidates pool and spa safety requirements (Part 9A not read). Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3
officialReferences.covers: Building Practice Note SP 02 (VBA), Version 3, published 26 September 2023. No review date is stated. Defines a pool as capable of containing water to a depth greater than 300 mm, and says the definition also covers spas and relocatable structures. Does not cover site fencing, barrier timing during construction, filling a concrete pool, a surveyor's certificate, a 14-day fencing notice, or the 12-month and six-month limits. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.

officialReferences.title: Pool safety barriers (Victorian Building Authority consumer page)
officialReferences.covers: States that a pool safety barrier must be capable of containing water to a depth greater than 300 mm, and that pools and spas that cannot hold water deeper than 300 mm are exempt; that safety barriers must comply with AS1926.1-2012; and that pools, spas and barriers must be constructed by a builder registered in an appropriate category or class, or by an owner-builder holding an owner-builder certificate of consent. Shows no published or updated date. Does not mention barrier timing during construction, a surveyor's certificate before a concrete pool is filled, a 14-day notice for a separate fencing contractor, or the 12-month start and six-month finish limits. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 01, Swimming pool standards and safety requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 2.0
officialReferences.pageDate: Published 27 April 2023 (Version 2.0); no later update date shown in the text read
officialReferences.covers: Read on 2026-11-03 (summary fetch of the PDF). Says the excavation of a pool shell can be a hazard; that site fencing considered under regulation 116 must include provisions to restrict access during excavation, during construction and once the pool can contain water; that where the relevant building surveyor determines protection work is required it must be provided before and during construction; that the barrier could be installed and inspected immediately after excavation is completed; that the relevant building surveyor must issue a Certificate of Pool and Spa Barrier Compliance (Form 23) with the final inspection or occupancy permit for council registration; and that building work for a pool and barrier must commence within 12 months of the building permit issue date and be completed within six months of commencement (regulations 53 and 54). Does not cover filling a concrete pool, builder registration, or a 14-day notice for a separate fencing contractor. The regulations themselves were not read. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.

officialReferences.title: Swimming Pool Requirements under the Building Regulations 2018: Council and Practitioner Guide (Victorian Building Authority), Version 1, hosted by Glenelg Shire Council
officialReferences.covers: Read on 2026-11-03 (summary fetch). Does not cover barrier timing during construction, filling, construction-site fencing, builder registration or the time limits for building work. Its 14-day periods (registration notice, barrier notices and certificate lodgement) are council registration periods, so they do not support the 14-day notice for a separate fencing contractor. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority, hosted by Glenelg Shire Council.
